leads.work: Unaccounted meter flow / 'Strangers Gas' cleanup: Logistics (Clem Cernosek) sends a memo for each meter with flow but no deal or an expired deal. The trader has to print it, sign it and return the original, choosing to extend the deal, create a new deal or write the volume off to Unaccounted for Gas. Volume Management then moves the volume to the write-off contract by hand.
leads.why: There are dozens of near-identical templated memos, many for tiny volumes (9–18 MMBtu) going back to 1999. A paper signature is required for each one, and follow-up messages confirm manual moves to contract 012-41500-02-004. This looks like a candidate for an automated exception report, a write-off threshold and electronic approval.

leads.work: Requests to extend expired deals or create new deal tickets when a meter flows after its deal ends (schedulers asking the trader meter by meter, every month).
leads.why: Aimee Lannou, Mary Poorman, Michael Olsen, Tom Acton and Karen Lindley send repeated one-off emails ('please extend deal X or create new'). Deals expire while gas keeps flowing, and a suspended counterparty blocks the extension. Auto-rollover of evergreen deals or an exception queue could remove this.

leads.work: Daily credit report forwarding: the credit group emails a daily Credit Report listing deals to rebook to the correct counterparty entity, and the book admin forwards each one by hand to a team member who rebooks the deals.
leads.why: Almost every business day there is a 'Credit Report--date' email, and Giron forwards each one manually to Carole Frank, sometimes several days' worth in a batch. Each report has 30+ rebook lines. Separately, Derek Bailey and Lesli Campbell send one-off rebook requests. This suggests counterparty mapping errors at deal entry and manual relay of the reports.

leads.work: Flipping Canadian counterparty deals (Duke, Dynegy Canada, Aquila Canada, Engage) into the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book by hand so they settle with ECC; repeated reminders from Stacey Vallejo.
leads.why: These requests recur and are deadline-driven, needed before invoicing and Nymex close. Stacey notes that an EOL auto-booking program for Duke exists for other counterparties but hasn't been set up yet. Book admins must search their books for missed deals.

leads.work: Monthly Arthur Andersen audit requests for P&L top pages, P&L drivers, origination support (deal tickets, confirmations, forward detail) and new-deal testing, passed down through the risk managers.
leads.why: These are 'monthly testing' requests. Giron forwards them to staff repeatedly ('AA is all over me today'). The same request goes to many desk heads each month.

leads.work: Counterparty MTM valuation requests from Confirmations (for counterparties' auditors), which need a Risk person to run and redact mini-books by hand.
leads.why: Joe Hunter says 'we receive several per week'. Confirmations has no valuation system access and plans to build EnTelligence with back-dated curves to take this off Risk.

leads.work: Origination schedule upkeep: a daily origination report for Fred Lagrasta, including $0-origination deals, plus corrections when origination is coded to the wrong group (West Gas Orig vs Middle Market) and double counting.
leads.why: A new daily report needs manual entry of many fields per deal, and later corrections are required. Origination data is maintained by hand in a file.

leads.work: Weekend on-call notes: by-hand logs of pipeline cuts (PG&E, Channel, Oasis), calls to gas control and re-noms, plus centralizing emailed nominations into a shared mailbox with manual filing.
leads.why: There are recurring weekly On-Call Notes emails and long phone-call logs. A new HPL.Scheduling mailbox relies on moving each nomination to a folder by hand to track status.

leads.work: Monthly OPM hours survey: managers enter their cost center's hours and activities each month, with reminders.
leads.why: This is a recurring monthly survey sent to about 50 managers with reminder emails. The SAP cost center conversion forced information to be re-entered by hand.

leads.work: Meter allocation and payment disputes (e.g., Alpine at meter 5892, Richardson, Copano, PG&E/TECO netting, Cleco/Torch). Long chains between scheduling, volume management, settlements and measurement where confirmed volumes don't match actual flow.
leads.why: These are multi-week threads with escalation ('I NEED HELP'), temporary reallocations and recoverable items. Scheduled and flowed volumes don't reconcile, and knowledge is lost when staff leave.

leads.work: Recurring manual price changes on specific deals (Enervest S#27239 rate changed 'as usual' each month; Agave pricing spreadsheet updates).
leads.why: 'As usual' means monthly manual repricing of the same deal, with reminder emails when it is late. Agave price discrepancies need the spreadsheet sent over by hand.

leads.work: Daily curves and P&L/DPR distribution: emailing daily curves to JPMorgan, physical forward detail, Enovate DPR approvals and prior-day P&L top pages.
leads.why: These are daily outbound files sent by hand (with wrong-address and forgot-attachment resends) and daily DPR approvals.

leads.work: System bridge/linkage gaps between EOL, Sitara, TAGG, SCI and TDS: missing cross-reference numbers, hedges not linking, deals unwound in TAGG but not Sitara, TDS flags and book mappings maintained by hand.
leads.why: Users praise the automatic bridge for saving bidweek time but still ask for Sitara/Tagg number links. Unwinds now need manual signatures. TDS book setup and region mapping are done by email. Desk-level summaries are misentered and cause SAP seller-rule adjustments.

leads.work: Manual booking of complex structured deals (virtual storage) that risk systems can't handle, with legs split across books and volumes adjusted weekly or monthly.
leads.why: Tomaski: 'our risk management systems will not handle this kind of a transaction without a lot of manual manipulation'. Giron expects twice as many legs plus weekly adjustments.

leads.work: Hiring and analyst rotation admin: repeated forms giving location, cost center and supervisor for each analyst, interview scheduling and passing resumes along.
leads.why: Many emails re-send the same data fields to HR for each analyst. Interviews are scheduled two interviewers at a time across seven people.

leads.work: Transition of Texas off-system pipeline rate work to another team, and transport rate/contract questions when contracts are renewed.
leads.why: Work is being handed between teams, the new owner has 'no idea what this entails', and rate questions come up when contracts are renumbered.
